title: Burst Shielding: Eviction Lanes and Soft-Admission for Multi-Region Load Shedding
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and implement a ‘Burst Shielding’ admission layer that protects core SLOs during transient spikes by routing traffic into tiered eviction lanes and applying soft-admission signals to clients. This ticket covers the admission policy, lane definitions, KV-cache-aware eviction heuristics, region-aware circuit-breaker integration, and the graceful degradation modes (response slimming, partial outputs, and early hinting). The goal is to limit high-latency and OOM incidents during bursts while preserving a best-effort experience for lower-priority traffic and enabling deterministic multi-region failover behavior.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Kickoff with reliability and serving runtime: agreed to prototype 3-lane model (critical, standard, best-effort) with separate token budgets and latency SLO targets per lane.

2026-02-18 - Design review: PM requested explicit client SDK soft-admission signal (early_hint + degrade_code) and a telemetry schema for per-tenant budget burn rate. Action: add telemetry event names and update SDK contract.

2026-02-25 - Engineering spike: implemented a simulator that replays production trace for burst scenarios. Findings: short eviction window (200ms) + long-term budget produces best SLO preservation; KV cache should be warmed for critical lane to avoid regression.

acceptance_criteria: Admission controller implements 3 configurable lanes with per-lane token/req budgets and eviction policies
Clients receive an early_hint header when soft-admission is applied and a degrade_code indicating chosen degradation mode
Telemetry emits per-tenant lane decisions, burn rate, and cumulative evictions to Grafana
Multi-region failover respects lane budgets and triggers region-level circuit-breaker before global overload
End-to-end integration test that replays production burst trace shows <= 2x increase in P99 latency for critical lane and <10% request drop for standard lane
Runbook updated and on-call can adjust thresholds via Console knobs without code deploy
implementation_notes: Admission algorithm: maintain per-tenant sliding window counters (token tokens) plus short-term fast-path counter for burst shakeouts
Eviction lanes: Critical (latency SLO prioritized, KV cache pinned), Standard (best-effort latency), Best-effort (aggressive slimming & reject)
Soft-admission modes: response_slim (truncate tokens + compress), structured_fallback (return summary/embedding), reject_with_hint (429 with Retry-After + degrade_code)

Circuit-breaker integration: layer a region-capacity vector; when region-level burn rate > 1.5x, prefer redirecting Standard/Best-effort to secondary region, escalate to reject if both regions overloaded
KV cache heuristic: avoid evicting cached prompts in Critical lane; allow trimming KV for Standard and Best-effort lanes first
Telemetry: emit 'admission.decision' events with fields (tenant, lane, decision, reason, pre_burst_slo, post_burst_slo_estimate) - follow existing schema in infra-telemetry
Client SDK contract: add client-side handler for early_hint header and degrade_code to show graceful fallback UX and optionally retry after backoff
Operational controls: Console will expose per-tenant multipliers and emergency 'shield' toggle to instantly flip non-critical lanes to reject-only for incident mitigation
